findings.title: Success criteria coverage and sequencing
findings.description:
- **Auto-init:** fresh-clone `cf build` (and `--json`) is covered by T17–T21; the out-of-sync warning by T17/T18/T21.
- **`cf guides info`:** read-only checkout reporting is covered by T11/T24.
- **Rename and `--strategy`:** the `manual` alias (flag and config) is covered by T1–T8; `cf init --strategy` and the help text by T25–T27.
- **Managed-directory notice and docs:** T28–T30.
- **Malformed config fails install:** T5/T6(c).
- **Literal and catch greps:** T3/T5/T32.
- **CHANGELOG/DEVLOG:** T31.

Nothing is out of scope. The design restates no NFR, so no load-test or CI-gating task is needed.

findings.title: Real-git fixture tests are placed in test files that module-mock `fs` and `gitExec`
findings.description:
- **Tests that can't run where they're placed:** T18 puts its fixture tests in `GuideManager.test.ts` ("fixture `cloned()`, assert directory populated"). T12 and T16 add fixture tests next to the existing detector and strategy tests. But `GuideManager.test.ts:7-48` uses hoisted `vi.mock` for `fs`, `gitExec`, `GuideDetector` and `SubmoduleStrategy`. `GuideDetector.test.ts:7-12` and `SubmoduleStrategy.test.ts:5-10` mock `fs` and `gitExec` too. A real temp repo can't work in those files.
- **Wrong pointer:** the Context Summary (line 50) and T9 ("extend it rather than duplicating") say `SubmoduleStrategy.test.ts` already has a real-git temp-repo pattern. It doesn't: no file in `packages/core/tests/guides/` uses `mkdtemp` or real git.
- **Fix:** name a separate integration test file, e.g. `packages/core/tests/guides/checkout.integration.test.ts`, with no module mocks, for the fixture cases in T12, T16 and T18. Correct the pointer in the Context Summary.
- **Missing detail in T9:** git 2.38.1 and later refuses local-path submodules unless `protocol.file.allow=always` is set. The fixture's `submodule add`, and the `submodule update --init` inside `SubmoduleStrategy.init()`, will fail with "transport 'file' not allowed" unless the test sets it. Because `gitExec` builds on the process environment, the test can set it through `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`/`GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0`/`GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0`. T9 should say so.

findings.title: T13/T14 assume a `/timed out/i` network pattern that doesn't exist
findings.description:
- **The claim:** T13 says "the `/timed out/i` pattern already matches", repeating design D10. T14 expects the timeout rejection to contain `GUIDE_OFFLINE_REMEDIATION`.
- **The code:** `NETWORK_ERROR_PATTERNS` has `/connection timed out/i` and `/etimedout/i`, not `/timed out/i`. A message like "git command timed out after 60 seconds" matches neither, so no remediation text is appended and T14 fails.
- **Fix:** T13 should either word the message to match an existing pattern or add a single `/timed out/i` entry to the list. Adding the entry is one line and matches what the design intends.

findings.title: T11 makes `detect()` throw on `'error'`, which the design does not specify
findings.description:
- **The mismatch:** the design's Data Flow throws on `'error'` inside `ensureCheckout()`. T11 instead throws from `GuideDetector.detect()`.
- **Why it matters:** `detect()` backs read-only commands (`cf guides info`, `guide_status`, setup-ide). With T11, a submodule project on a machine where `git submodule status` fails would break `cf guides info`, which works today. That cuts against the design's "a user can always inspect first" mitigation.
- **Hidden test fallout:** `detect()` gains a new `gitExec` call, but `GuideDetector.test.ts` mocks `gitExec`. Existing submodule-method detect tests will get a mock result they weren't written for, and no task says to update them.
- **Fix:** have T11 record the error state, or leave `checkout` null with a reason, and keep the throw in T17's `ensureCheckout()`. Add a T12 bullet to adjust the existing mocked detect tests.

findings.title: Contradictory rules on where the `manual` literal may appear
findings.description:
- **Three versions of the rule:**
  - T1 says `normalizeGuideMethod()` is "the only place the `manual` alias is spelled in source outside the `ConfigKeys` enum".
  - T7's grep allows the MCP zod enum entry and the deprecation-message text.
  - T32 re-checks the design's stricter "no `'manual'` outside the alias table and enum".
- **Result:** the implementer will get a failing check in T32 for code that T7 told them to write.
- **Fix:** have T7 build the MCP enum and the deprecation message from `GUIDE_METHOD_DEPRECATED_ALIASES`, so the literal really exists in one place. Or state one allowed list and use it in T1, T7 and T32.

findings.title: T5 doesn't cover the path with no `configManager`
findings.description:
- **The gap:** `resolveStrategy()` and `resolveSource()` only read config `if (this.configManager)`. When there is no manager they return the literal default.
- **Why it matters:** T5 says to delete the `'submodule'` literal because "an unset key already yields the `ConfigKeys` default". That's only true when a manager exists. A junior implementer will either leave the function with no return or bring back a hidden fallback.
- **Fix:** T5 should say to read `ConfigKeys['guide.git_strategy'].default` directly in the no-manager branch (D6). T6(a) should cover both "unset key" and "no manager".

findings.title: Commit points are written inside checkbox items, not as `**Commit**:` lines
findings.description:
- **The problem:** commit messages are embedded in `[ ] Success criteria:` sub-items. The project convention is to commit only at plain `**Commit**:` lines, and to commit at every top-level task when a file has none. As written, an implementer following the rule would make about 32 commits, not the intended 14.
- **The points themselves are fine:** every one sits at a tested, green state.
- **Fix:** move each commit to its own plain `**Commit**: <message>` line after the task.

findings.title: The config-file deprecation warning is never checked at the CLI
findings.description:
- **The criterion:** "shared config has `guide.git_strategy: manual` installs as tarball with the same warning."
- **What's tested:** T6(b) only checks that core reports the alias. T8 and walkthrough step 3 only use the `--strategy` flag. Nothing checks that `guidesInstallAction()` prints the warning on stderr for the config case, which T7's second bullet implements.
- **Fix:** add one case to T8.

findings.title: Some tasks are too small to verify on their own
findings.description:
- **Broken in between:** T10 can't pass typecheck until T11 ("typecheck passes once Task 11 populates the field"). The core test suite is red between T3 and T4.
- **Suggested merges:**
  - T10 into T11
  - T4 into T3
  - T13 with T14
  - T28 with T29

  This takes the file from 32 tasks to about 28 and keeps the test-with pattern. The total size is otherwise reasonable for a slice that touches core, CLI and MCP.

findings.title: T15's timeout default is ambiguous
findings.description:
- **The ambiguity:** the first bullet says `init()` always uses `GUIDE_INIT_TIMEOUT_MS`. The second says the timeout is an `init()` option so that `sync()` stays unbounded. It doesn't say whether the timeout is on or off when the option is left out.
- **Fix:** state it, e.g. "`init(path, { timeoutMs? })`; `ensureCheckout` passes `GUIDE_INIT_TIMEOUT_MS`, `sync()` passes nothing." That keeps the D10 constant at a single call site.
